name: Isolated Pulmonary Artery Sling

criteria.description: Left pulmonary artery arises anomalously from the right pulmonary artery
Compression of the trachea or esophagus by the anomalous pulmonary artery
No other significant congenital heart defects present (isolated form)
Confirmation by imaging modalities such as CT angiography or MRI

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anomalous origin of the left pulmonary artery from the right pulmonary artery with imaging confirmation and evidence of vascular compression
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other associated cardiac anomalies to classify as isolated.

laboratory: Generally normal laboratory tests; no specific biomarkers
imaging: CT angiography showing anomalous origin of left pulmonary artery from right pulmonary artery
MRI angiography confirming vascular sling and airway compression
Bronchoscopy revealing tracheal compression and possible tracheomalacia
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Echocardiography to exclude associated cardiac anomalies
Pulmonary function tests may show obstructive pattern in older children

distinguishingFeatures: Other vascular rings involve different arterial anomalies such as double aortic arch
May have different clinical presentations and imaging findings
Diagnosis confirmed by bronchoscopy without vascular anomaly

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress with stridor unresponsive to medical therapy
Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties and airway obstruction
references: Backer CL, Mavroudis C. Pulmonary artery sling: a comprehensive review. Semin Thorac Cardiovasc Surg Pediatr Card Surg Annu. 2004;7:56-66.
